subject: Social Studies
stem: The President of India can be removed from office before the end of the term only through a process, initiated in either House of Parliament on a charge of 'violation of the Constitution', that requires a resolution passed by a two-thirds majority of the total membership of that House and then investigated/agreed to by the other House. This process is called:
explanation: Under Article 61, impeachment of the President requires a special majority (two-thirds of total membership, not just those present and voting) in both Houses on the specific ground of constitutional violation — unlike a No-Confidence Motion (against the Council of Ministers, simple majority, Lok Sabha only).

subject: Social Studies
stem: Judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts in India are appointed through a system, evolved via Supreme Court judgments (the 'Judges Cases') rather than being explicitly written in the Constitution, in which a body of senior judges headed by the Chief Justice of India recommends names to the government. This system is known as the:
explanation: The Collegium System, established through the Second and Third Judges Cases, gives the judiciary primacy in appointing/transferring judges; the NJAC, created by a 2014 constitutional amendment to replace it with government involvement, was struck down by the Supreme Court in 2015 as unconstitutional.
